elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal: a signal head whose state values include circular_red and green_arrow(dir), and 'several states may be displayed at once'; 'a steady red with a green turn arrow' is a head h displaying circular_red together with green_arrow(dir) for some dir in {left, right, straight, u_turn}, and not circular_green. 'the signal' is the head the subject faces (s3), and the highway it controls is fixed under s4.

'Pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), claimed by id and never expanded.

'facing such a signal': the same head h as s1 ('such a signal'). With D the vector from the subject's position (kin.position) to h's location (dev.position, 'location of the device head / sign face') and H the subject's heading (kin.heading, read normalised): H·D > 0, (H·D)² ≥ p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos² · |D|², and |D|² ≤ p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach². The head's position is used for facing only, never as a stand-in for a stop line or a crossing (dev.position's 'not a stand-in' clause). The head is tied to the subject not by this comparison but by the relations of s4 (dev.governs, st.on_way, st.lane_enters) to the roadway whose occupancy by the subject (rel.occupies) the duty reads.

'shall not enter the highway': 'Highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095) is 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way', st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'). A pedestrian facing the signal already stands on a highway (its sidewalk), so entering is read as its footprint coming to overlap (rel.occupies) a st.roadway ('the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic') r lying on that highway w (st.on_way(r, w)), not having overlapped r at the previous observation (narrowing below). 'the highway' is the one at 'the signal': w is a highway that the head h controls — some travel region g (st.travel_region, the abstract kind of what a device can govern) with dev.governs(h, g) lies on w (st.on_way(g, w)), or g enters an intersection i (st.lane_enters(g, i), st.intersection) that lies on w (st.on_way(i, w): 'an intersection lies on every way that meets there'); where h governs the intersection itself, g is i. This ties the head to the roadway the subject enters through relation atoms, never through distance (dev.governs: 'the region a device governs is not where a halt is required' — it is used here for which highway the signal controls, not for a place of halt).

'unless permitted to proceed by another device as provided in NRS 484B.283' borrows the permissions 283 sets forth for pedestrian signals (dev.pedestrian_signal, state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}, countdown attribute). From NRS-484B-283-1d1: 'While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal' — a pedestrian head d showing walk that the subject faces (kin.position, kin.heading, dev.position of d with p.ped_signal_facing_cos and p.ped_signal_facing_reach), governing (dev.governs) the roadway r entered or a lane (st.lane) the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies): the crossing 'in the direction of the signal'. From NRS-484B-283-1d2: 'While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer, a pedestrian may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal' — the same with d showing dont_walk_flashing with its countdown attribute true. From NRS-484B-283-1d3: 'a pedestrian who entered the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) [NRS-484B-283-1d1] may continue to cross the highway' and NRS-484B-283-1d4: 'a pedestrian who entered the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) or (2) [NRS-484B-283-1d1, NRS-484B-283-1d2] may continue to cross the highway' — the subject continuing a crossing: its latest step from a sidewalk (st.sidewalk) onto a roadway or lane was made under walk (or, for (1)(d)(4), under the countdown) at a head governing that roadway or lane which it faced, it has overlapped no sidewalk since, and a head governing that roadway or lane now shows dont_walk_flashing without countdown ((1)(d)(3), entry under walk) or dont_walk_steady ((1)(d)(4), entry under walk or countdown). The qualification 283 itself retains, 'Except as otherwise provided in NRS 484B.287, 484B.290 and 484B.350', is kept by the 'unless' compositions on this span.

compositions.quote: While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal

While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer, a pedestrian may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal

While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated and flashing but is not accompanied by a countdown timer, a pedestrian may not proceed to cross the highway, but a pedestrian who entered the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) [NRS-484B-283-1d1] may continue to cross the highway

While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated and steady a pedestrian may not proceed to cross the highway, but a pedestrian who entered the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) or (2) [NRS-484B-283-1d1, NRS-484B-283-1d2] may continue to cross the highway

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian). At the judged observation there are: a traffic signal head h (dev.traffic_signal) displaying circular_red together with green_arrow(dir) for some dir in {left, right, straight, u_turn}, and not circular_green; the subject faces h: with D the vector from the subject's kin.position to h's dev.position and H the subject's kin.heading, H·D > 0, (H·D)² ≥ p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos² · (Dx² + Dy²), and Dx² + Dy² ≤ p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach²; a highway w (st.highway) that h controls: some travel region g (st.travel_region) with dev.governs(h, g) and either st.on_way(g, w), or some intersection i (st.intersection) with st.lane_enters(g, i) and st.on_way(i, w) (where g is itself an intersection it lies on every way that meets there); and a roadway r (st.roadway) with st.on_way(r, w) that the subject's footprint did not overlap (rel.occupies) at the previous observation. Excepted (s5), for that r: the subject is permitted to proceed by a pedestrian signal as provided in NRS 484B.283, that is, (a) some pedestrian head d (dev.pedestrian_signal) showing walk that the subject faces governs (dev.governs) r or a lane (st.lane) the subject's footprint overlaps at the judged observation; or (b) the same with d showing dont_walk_flashing with its countdown attribute true; or (c) the subject is continuing a crossing it began lawfully: its latest step from a sidewalk onto a roadway or lane (the latest observation before the judged one at which its footprint came to overlap a roadway or lane, having overlapped a sidewalk (st.sidewalk) at the observation before; history bound: that step, searched back without other limit) was made while a pedestrian head e governing that roadway or lane, which the subject faced, showed walk, or showed dont_walk_flashing with its countdown; its footprint has overlapped no sidewalk at any observation since that step; and at the judged observation e shows dont_walk_flashing without its countdown attribute (entry under walk only, (1)(d)(3)) or dont_walk_steady (entry under walk or under the countdown, (1)(d)(4)); where that step lies before the recording, (c) is unknown. Facing a pedestrian head d is read with p.ped_signal_facing_cos and p.ped_signal_facing_reach in the same form as facing h. The permission of (a)–(c) does not hold where NRS 484B.283's own exceptions are engaged ('Except as otherwise provided in NRS 484B.287, 484B.290 and 484B.350'): where the subject is engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A, LVMC_11_30_060_B, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2 (subject mapped to subject), or some vehicle v of the scene is engaged by LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2 (their subject mapped to v).
obligation: For every roadway r selected again with the applicability's whole selection (a head h displaying circular_red with a green arrow and not circular_green that the subject faces; a highway w that h controls through a travel region g it governs lying on w or entering an intersection lying on w; r on w; the subject's footprint not overlapping r at the previous observation; and the s5 permission not holding for r): the subject's footprint does not overlap r at the judged observation — it has not entered the highway.

narrowings.why: A pedestrian facing the signal already stands on the highway (its sidewalk); entering the highway is read as entering the roadway, the part of the highway it is not yet on.

'the highway' is read as a highway the signal controls: one on which a travel region the head governs lies, or one that meets at the intersection such a region enters (st.on_way, st.lane_enters, dev.governs); a roadway of a highway the head neither governs nor meets at its intersection is not 'the highway' of this signal.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Highway A (north–south) and highway B (east–west) meet at intersection i. Head h on the far side of i governs the northbound lane of A, which enters i, and displays circular_red with green_arrow(left). A pedestrian on the southwest corner sidewalk heads north, facing h within reach and within the facing angle; no pedestrian signal is present. The pedestrian steps into B's roadway west of i (a roadway on B, which i lies on): its footprint comes to overlap it.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the pedestrian remains on the sidewalk while h displays the red with the arrow.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but h displays circular_green alone; the pedestrian steps into B's roadway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but h's position is not observed (dev.position absent), so whether the pedestrian faces it is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but a pedestrian head across B's crosswalk, governing B's roadway west of i and faced by the pedestrian, shows walk: the pedestrian is permitted to proceed under NRS 484B.283(1)(d)(1).

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As in branch_1, but the pedestrian head shows dont_walk_flashing with its countdown: permitted under NRS 484B.283(1)(d)(2).

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As in branch_1, but the pedestrian head shows dont_walk_steady: no device permits the pedestrian to proceed, and it steps into B's roadway.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the roadway the pedestrian steps into lies on a highway C that carries no region h governs and does not meet at i; h governs only A's northbound lane entering i.

scenarios.name: branch_5
scenarios.narrative: B is a divided highway with two roadways separated by a median. The pedestrian, facing a pedestrian head governing both roadways, stepped from the sidewalk onto B's first roadway while it showed walk, crossed to the median without touching a sidewalk, and now, with the pedestrian head showing dont_walk_steady and h displaying circular_red with green_arrow(left) ahead of it, steps into B's second roadway: it is continuing a crossing begun lawfully under NRS 484B.283(1)(d)(4).

param_proposals.name: p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about thirty degrees) between a pedestrian's heading and the line from its position to a vehicular signal head at which the pedestrian counts as facing that head: the lateral offset of a far-side head from the crossing's line plus a pedestrian's heading wander
param_proposals.source: MUTCD far-side signal head placement and pedestrian heading variability

param_proposals.name: p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach
param_proposals.convention: the largest distance from a pedestrian to a vehicular signal head at which the head counts as one the pedestrian faces across the intersection: a wide urban intersection (about 40 m) plus the set-back of a far-side head beyond the far crosswalk
param_proposals.source: urban intersection dimensions and MUTCD far-side head placement
